stories.original:
**UK open banking passes one billion payments and 100 billion API calls**

*The milestone underscores open banking's shift from regulatory experiment to scaled payment infrastructure, though the path to open finance remains uncertain.*

Open banking payments in the UK have crossed the one billion mark, with cumulative API calls surpassing 100 billion, according to data reported this week. Variable recurring payments are a growing contributor, with the UK Payments Initiative now operating a commercial scheme and firms such as Modulr already live with commercial VRP products.

The raw numbers confirm that open banking has reached genuine scale as a payment rail. But volume growth alone does not resolve the structural questions around the ecosystem's next phase. The UK's open finance consultation, announced by chancellor Rachel Reeves on July 14, is still at an early stage, and the commercial model for broader data sharing beyond payments remains undefined. The Financial Conduct Authority's roadmap targets 2030 for investment data, but intermediary steps – particularly around liability, standards and consent – are largely unresolved.

For infrastructure operators and third-party providers, the billion-payment threshold is operationally significant: it raises the bar on API resilience, token security and real-time monitoring at a scale that the original Open Banking Implementation Entity framework was not designed to handle.

*Sources: [Open banking payments exceed one billion mark](https://www.computerweekly.com/news/366646532/Open-banking-payments-exceed-one-billion-mark) — Computer Weekly | [UK Open Banking Hits 100B API Calls and 1B Payments Milestone](https://www.bobsguide.com/uk-open-banking-hits-100b-api-calls-and-1b-payments-milestone/) — bobsguide*

stories.original:
**ECB commits to highest accessibility standards for digital euro app**

*The European Central Bank has published accessibility requirements for the digital euro app, signalling that design choices for the pilot phase are advancing toward implementation detail.*

Accessibility standards published by the European Central Bank (ECB) on July 30 set out detailed usability requirements for the digital euro app, covering people with disabilities and those with limited digital literacy. The commitment applies to both the app interface and associated offline functionality.

The announcement arrives as the digital euro moves through its pilot phase, with 36 payment providers selected in July to participate. The full European Parliament voted on July 9 to approve a negotiating mandate for the digital euro regulation, after the economic affairs committee endorsed the text on June 23. The legislative framework and technical design work are now running in parallel. Accessibility requirements at this stage indicate the ECB is making binding design commitments before the legislative text is finalised, a sequencing choice that could constrain or accelerate the Parliament's negotiating position.

For payment service providers already selected for the pilot, the accessibility standards add a layer of product specification that will shape development timelines and cost. The commitment also addresses a recurring concern from consumer groups and the European Parliament that the digital euro must serve populations currently underserved by digital payment tools.

*Sources: [Digital euro app to incorporate highest accessibility standards](https://www.ecb.europa.eu//press/pr/date/2026/html/ecb.pr260730~3b3bfbb565.en.html) — ECB*

stories.original:
**Plend secures £50m lending facility backed by open banking credit models**

*The UK lender's funding deal with Triple Point illustrates how open banking data is becoming a bankable asset class for credit underwriting.*

Plend, a UK-based lender that uses open banking data and proprietary credit technology to assess affordability, has secured a lending facility of up to £50 million from Triple Point. The facility will fund loan originations underwritten using transaction-level banking data rather than traditional credit bureau scores alone.

Open banking data is moving from a supplementary input to a primary underwriting signal. Plend's model uses consumer-permissioned account data to assess income, spending patterns and affordability in real time, positioning it within a cohort of lenders – including Abound and others – that treat open banking as core infrastructure for credit decisions rather than an overlay on existing bureau data.

Triple Point's willingness to back a facility of this size on open banking-derived underwriting suggests institutional capital is increasingly comfortable with the data's reliability and predictive value. If lending facilities scale on the back of account data, the commercial incentive to standardise and extend data sharing frameworks grows accordingly.

*Sources: [Plend secures up to £50m facility from Triple Point](https://fintech.global/2026/07/29/plend-secures-up-to-50m-facility-from-triple-point/) — FinTech Global*

stories.original:
**MoonPay launches payment vault enabling AI agents to transact autonomously**

*PayBox lets AI agents execute payments within conversations, adding to the growing infrastructure layer for agentic commerce across fiat and digital assets.*

MoonPay's new product, PayBox, is a payment vault that supports both fiat and digital asset rails, positioning it at the intersection of agentic commerce and crypto payments infrastructure. The tool allows AI agents to initiate and complete transactions on behalf of users without leaving a conversational interface, with pre-authorised spending limits and asset types governing what agents can do.

The launch extends a pattern visible across 2026: Visa's partnership with OpenAI, ING's completion of Europe's first agentic payment with Worldline and Mastercard, and Crédit Agricole's production agentic transaction in France have all moved agent-initiated payments from concept to live deployment. MoonPay's entry is distinct in that it bridges fiat and crypto rails within a single agent-facing product, rather than operating solely within card network or account-to-account frameworks.

For European payment providers watching the agentic commerce space, the question is less whether AI agents will initiate payments and more which rails and identity frameworks will govern those transactions. PayBox's architecture – a vault model where users pre-authorise spending limits and asset types – offers one answer, but regulatory clarity on agent liability and consent remains thin across all jurisdictions.

*Sources: [MoonPay opens PayBox for AI agent transactions](https://www.finextra.com/pressarticle/110532/moonpay-opens-paybox-for-ai-agent-transactions?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra*

**RunPay receives Moldovan authorisation to provide open banking services**

*Moldova's central bank has licensed its first open banking provider, extending PSD2-aligned frameworks into south-eastern Europe's smaller markets.*

RunPay has received authorisation from the National Bank of Moldova to provide open banking services, making it the first provider licensed under the country's framework for consumer-permissioned account data access. The authorisation requires RunPay to meet defined technical and security standards before accessing customer data held by banks.

Moldova's adoption of open banking infrastructure follows the broader pattern of EU-adjacent markets aligning domestic frameworks with Payment Services Directive 2 (PSD2) principles ahead of potential EU accession or regulatory convergence. The country's financial sector is small – total banking assets are a fraction of those in neighbouring Romania – but the licensing decision signals that open banking is now a baseline regulatory expectation rather than a feature of advanced markets alone.

For providers operating across central and south-eastern Europe, Moldova's move incrementally expands the addressable market for cross-border open banking services and adds another jurisdiction to the patchwork of regulatory frameworks that Payment Services Directive 3 (PSD3) and the Financial Data Access regulation (FIDA) are intended, eventually, to harmonise.

*Sources: [RunPay receives National Bank of Moldova authorisation to provide Open Banking services](https://thepaypers.com/fintech/news/runpay-receives-national-bank-of-moldova-authorisation-to-provide-open-banking-services) — Thepaypers*
